newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army says it killed 126 returning refugees.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army says it killed 126 returning refugees.

text.p: Soldiers from Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army shot dead 126 Burundian Hutu refugees who had been expelled from Tanzania and tried to escape from a detention centre in Burundi, an army spokesman said on Saturday.
Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi told Reuters the 126 refugees were killed late on Friday. "They were all shot and killed after they tried to escape from the centre," he said.
Nibizi condemned the killing, which took place in the northeast province of Muyinga, and said seven soldiers involved in the shooting had been arrested.
"The seven soldiers involved in the shootings have all been arrested and will be charged before courts of law," Nibizi said in a rare admission of wrongdoing by the army.
Burundi is at war between the army and Hutu rebels fighting for a greater political stake in the tiny tea and coffee-growing country whose government and army are dominated by the Tutsi minority.

Nibizi's comments came shortly after the head of the U.N. refugee agency in Burundi, Hitoshi Mise, told Reuters that some 120 Burundian Hutu refugees accused of fomenting trouble in camps in Tanzania were expelled back to Burundi on Saturday.
But Nibizi said the expulsions took place on Friday.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in Burundi since the killing of its first freely elected Hutu president by renegade Tutsi soldiers in 1993.
Burundi's 25,000-strong army is overwhelmingly drawn from the Tutsi minority and has been accused by human rights organisations of committing massacres against the majority Hutus.
